newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian insurance industry troubles seen deepening.
newsitem.headline: Russian insurance industry troubles seen deepening.

text.p: Russia's deteriorating insurance industry showed poor results in the first quarter of the year, confirming a general industry decline, the head of the country's insurance supervisory body, said on Tuesday.

"In our opinion, the critical situation is continuing to deepen," Rosstrakhnadzor chief Valery Sukhov told an industry conference. "The volumes of premuims are falling, the number of companies is shrinking."
He said about 200 of Russia's 2,500 insurance companies reported no operations in the first quarter.
Sukhov said Rosstrakhnadzor had withdrawn 12 licences and was prepared to withdraw about 30 more.

In 1996 the volume of insurance premiums in Russia was 27.4 trillion roubles, 4.3 trillion roubles more than in 1995. But 1996 annual inflation of 22 percent meant 1996 was the first year since 1991 when premiums fell in real terms.
